name: filter-includes-minimum
why: a log at exactly the minimum level is filtered

name: filtered-logs-use-sequence-numbers
why: filtered logs still advance the sequence numbers

name: filtered-not-counted
why: filtered logs are not counted

name: sequence-starts-at-zero
why: the first sequence number is 0

name: lost-not-counted
why: logs that cannot be stored are not counted as lost

name: header-only-buffer-stores
why: a buffer of exactly 13 bytes stores an empty record

name: truncates-one-byte-too-many
why: the cut message is one byte shorter than what fits

name: truncated-not-counted
why: truncation is not counted

name: exact-fit-counts-as-truncated
why: a record that fills the buffer exactly counts as truncated

name: evicts-one-too-many
why: one extra record is evicted when the new one fits exactly

name: evicts-at-most-one
why: at most one old record is evicted

name: eviction-not-counted
why: evictions are not counted

name: write-position-ignores-head
why: the record is written at used_ instead of head_ + used_

name: write-does-not-wrap
why: write() drops the part that should continue at offset 0

name: read-does-not-wrap
why: read() stops at the end of the buffer and leaves the rest of the bytes as they were

name: sequence-stored-in-one-byte

why: only the low byte of the length is stored

name: length-stored-in-two-bytes
why: only two bytes of the length are stored

name: level-not-stored
why: the level is always stored as Debug

name: snapshot-newest-first
why: snapshot() returns the newest record first

name: dump-without-hash

name: clear-keeps-bytes
why: clear() forgets to reset the bytes in use
